---
applyTo: "packages/react/runtime/**"
---

When updating runtime snapshot tests for preview preact builds that carry named children props like `$0` and slot-index semantics, keep `list` host snapshots isolated from surrounding `view`/`text` snapshots by creating a standalone `__SNAPSHOT__(<list>{HOLE}</list>)` and inserting it into the outer snapshot.
To cover SSR hydration of coalesced list snapshots, use a `*.legacy-slot.test.jsx` fixture and assert that the list slot has a nonzero element index. List callbacks and recycling maps must use the element selected by `slot[0][1]`, while `__element_root` remains `__elements[0]` for parent insertion and removal. Clear all three native list callbacks before SSR hydration so callbacks from the server render cannot mask a missing or misplaced callback binding.
Default-slot SSR list coverage should assert an independent `ListSlotV2` snapshot at element index zero and preserve its slot index within its parent across hydration and updates. Mixed static and dynamic siblings can produce native wrapper elements; check their child placement rather than assuming a flat native tree. The SSR opcode decoder currently assumes every encoded snapshot and text node has native element references: encoding list items before their native elements are created produces null references and fails hydration in both slot modes. Treat partial native materialization as a separate compatibility gap from selecting the list's slot element.
Do not drop `packages/react/runtime/__test__/list.test.jsx` cases added on `main`; preserve nested-list recording and `__DestroyLifetime` callback cleanup assertions while adapting expectations to the new snapshot structure.
For ReactLynx `Children`, reuse `preact/compat` behavior and derive types from `typeof PreactChildren`; only override `map`, `forEach`, and `toArray` to expose readonly frozen arrays.
When adding snapshot runtime tests that manually construct `SnapshotInstance` or `BackgroundSnapshotInstance`, remember that the managers' `clear()` methods intentionally do not reset `nextId`; use explicit ids or restore `nextId` in the test to avoid unrelated inline snapshot churn.
Keep devtools Lepus helpers that only need snapshot instance lookup importing the minimal `snapshotInstanceManager` module instead of the full snapshot implementation, so the main-thread transform can retain the singleton without pulling unrelated snapshot runtime code.
Keep the Snapshot first-screen lifecycle envelope host-opaque: native and Web hosts relay `__OnLifecycleEvent` data but ReactLynx owns the nested serialized `root` contract. When changing that contract, version the root representation within ReactLynx, preserve legacy receive support, and hydrate the new representation directly instead of rebuilding the legacy object tree first.
When adding React runtime ALOG diagnostics, guard the entire formatting path with `typeof __ALOG__ !== 'undefined' && __ALOG__`, call `console.alog?.(...)`, and keep `JSON.stringify` inside the guard so disabled logging does not add serialization work.
Keep builtin attribute-name conversion for JSX spreads aligned across Snapshot and Element Template. Centralize attribute and event-key recognition in `src/shared/attribute-name.ts`; keep `transformAttrName` responsible only for name conversion and use `isEventPropKey` explicitly on the transformed name where event classification is required. When a React-style event key is renamed, emit the transformed native event key but preserve the original spread key in the event value so the background runtime can recover the handler. Keep `updateSpread` ordering stable; convert marked spread keys while collecting list-item platform info instead of moving the full spread transform ahead of list processing. Keep `extractListItemPlatformInfo` a pure filter for normalized attribute names: only values carrying the raw `__spread` marker should have their keys transformed, because known spread values without the marker may already be normalized and custom rename rules are not necessarily idempotent.
Read runtime build configuration from the page-scoped `lynx.__runtime_configs__`.
Keep runtime marker ownership aligned with bundle ownership: host runtime entries register the host backend and version, while standalone lazy `internal` shells call the host-exported registration APIs with the producer bundle's build-time constants. The host-side `lazy/import` modules only populate shared exports and must not register on behalf of standalone producers. In bundle tests, distinguish a real `.registerRuntimeVersion` property call from the bare identifier in an exports destructuring.
Send ctx-not-found diagnostics through sendCtxNotFoundEventToBackground(id, options), including the operation name, commitId, and isHydration (default false). For InsertBefore and RemoveChild, send one event with numeric parent/child IDs and missingNode (1 = parent, 2 = child, 3 = both), determined from main-thread contexts. Treat ID zero as valid.
Keep type lookup and message assembly inside reportCtxNotFound. Always include the primary snapshotType from data.id; read instance.type directly, falling back to null for missing instances or definitions. Infer the background parent for single-node errors. Derive parent/child missing booleans from missingNode and omit them when it is absent. Preserve the original no-JS-context error, and update runtime and testing-library snapshots when messages change.
Forward newly added React APIs from standalone lazy entries by destructuring the host export object, as with existing APIs. Avoid feature-specific missing-export assertion wrappers for MainThreadObject, including in its main-thread registration binding; lazy bundle and host version mismatches are a general compatibility problem to address centrally. Keep type-key and factory conflict checks in the runtime registry.
Preserve the lightweight `loadWorkletRuntime` compatibility export in Snapshot internal, lazy internal, and worklet-runtime bindings for precompiled consumers. Keep it independent of the module-graph initialization entry: importing the compatibility helper must not initialize or statically include the worklet runtime, and restoring it must not restore legacy chunk injection to the current toolchain.
Validate this compatibility with an old-toolchain fixture containing a real main-thread function; a background-only example does not exercise the loader. Freeze both the consumer and component-library bundles and swap only the ReactLynx external. For a cold-start web external fixture, provide its actual legacy worklet runtime chunk as a host resource in both control and patched runs; missing legacy chunks are a separate failure from a missing compatibility export.
When testing a lazy runtime's build-time `__RUNTIME_VERSION__` fallback, cover both stamped and missing versions. Separate ESM module loads can make V8 report a duplicate uncovered branch for that compile-time expression; keep any coverage ignore on that expression alone and verify the package's `test:snapshot` threshold.
Guard every runtime read of `__EXPERIMENTAL_TRANSFORM_BUILTIN_ATTRIBUTE_NAMES__` with `typeof __EXPERIMENTAL_TRANSFORM_BUILTIN_ATTRIBUTE_NAMES__ !== 'undefined'`. When combining this object-valued Define macro with a runtime boolean guard, put the macro before the runtime boolean so SWC reduces an enabled object config to the runtime boolean instead of emitting `runtimeFlag && 1`; cover disabled and object-config output shapes with production `define-dce` cases.
For `MainThreadObject`, keep initialization payload and realized-object types distinct, brand source-runtime handles with the runtime-owned `WeakSet`, and realize targets through a type-keyed registry. Define `create` as a capture-free Main Thread Function whose dependencies use shared-runtime imports, register its descriptor during MTS module evaluation, and ensure registration again on the first MTS hook use for runtimes that retain modules across a per-page registry reset. Check the capture-free contract only in development. Resolve each descriptor lazily once from the worklet map after compiler-appended worklet registration has run, without closure transformation or binding. Return an immutable type token without exposing the factory implementation or handle wire fields; expose source-side payload access only after an exact-type `downcast()` through the handle's readonly `creationPayload`. Treat the type key as the factory's compatibility identity and change it when payload or target semantics become incompatible. Preserve stable target identity through first-screen hydration, release redundant or abandoned strong references from runtime maps, and preserve weak target branding until garbage collection so releasing one handle cannot invalidate another live handle or capture of the same target; do not expose public semantic disposal. Do not attach React bookkeeping fields to third-party objects, and preserve the two-entry `MainThreadRef` wire tuple and untracked fast path when no object type is present.
For third-party stateful APIs that have different dual-thread semantics, expose the adapter from a dedicated `@lynx-js/*` companion package and map that package's public request by issuer layer in `plugin-react-alias`; do not add the third-party packages to `@lynx-js/react` dependencies. Keep main-thread implementations read-only for first-screen rendering: setters may report a development error but must not mutate, and effects or subscriptions must not execute callbacks. Preact Signals consumers import `@lynx-js/react-signals`; that package owns the Preact Signals dependencies and matching `lepus` implementation.
When changing worklet transformation or hydration, keep recovery metadata tied to the context actually owned by the bound function. Nested original contexts can become unreachable when their parent replaces them with callable functions; hydration must not depend on weak references to those originals. Root hydration receives the original context from the backend directly. Avoid reintroducing a cached function's strong reference to its original root context: PrimJS traces WeakMap values even when their keys are otherwise unreachable. Cover both state recovery after original-context collection and eventual context/caller release.

Keep Element Template MainThreadRef initialization on its own unversioned event, separate from render patches. Send pending initialization on background commits, including before hydration, and before dispatching hydration UI updates. Register and reset the initialization receiver independently from the UI patch receiver at the native runtime initialization/destruction entrypoints; resetting the UI patch listener must not unsubscribe ref initialization. Preserve initialization before delayed main-thread calls, and log its send/receive payloads only under `__ALOG__`. A stale UI patch must not cancel initialization, and a UI serialization error must not consume an otherwise valid ref initialization.
Keep dual-thread communication reload filtering inside core send and listener-registration helpers. Stamp outgoing messages with the current getReloadVersion(), and reject stale calls and return values before invoking their handlers. Worklet code keeps its original execution and listener locations without reading or passing version numbers. Registration delivers parsed payloads and returns cleanup bound to the actual registered callback; avoid a listener identity registry. Clear pending first-screen runOnBackground callbacks at the main-thread reload boundary before rendering the new page, for both Snapshot and Element Template. Preserve callbacks queued by the new render; do not add per-callback reload-version wrappers. Keep native patch entrypoints and task loops unchanged, keeping the separate ET ref initialization event unversioned. Do not filter GC release messages through the dual-thread communication envelope: they have a different lifetime.
Advance the ET main-thread version after old ref cleanup and before new rendering so unmount calls retain their old ownership. Cover real ordinary reload resets, delayed request delivery, and reused resolver IDs on both threads; a persistent worklet listener must read the same current reload state as the backend.

Keep Snapshot background-page cleanup in `destroyBackground`: disable global snapshot patch collection before unmounting, then call `resetSnapshotBackgroundFunctionRuntime` and `resetSnapshotMainThreadFunctionRuntime` after unmount and commit cleanup to clear retained background functions, their listeners, the delayed runOnMainThread queue, and return listeners, including registrations made by cleanup callbacks. Keep these resets in the Snapshot worklet ctx and runOnMainThread modules, matching ET's backend-specific helpers. Both ordinary reload and native page destruction must use this path; leave Element Template cleanup in its own backend.
For ET delayed-call reload regressions, queue calls before hydration and from an actual component unmount, run ordinary reload through the real hydration and patch listeners, and assert reused return IDs only complete the new call. Initialize the worklet runtime so the test executes the real task runner and return dispatch rather than injecting a return manually. The test harness shares resolver state across threads, so finish main-thread reload before registering the new background call.
For the equivalent Snapshot regression, deliver the real first-screen lifecycle event and apply the emitted `rLynxChange` payload. A manually dispatched return does not exercise old queued calls being packaged with the new reload version; assert the replacement Promise's value after executing that patch.
For Snapshot background-function reload coverage, obtain worklet contexts from the hydrated native event, execute actual runOnBackground requests and returns, and register a context from component unmount. Hold and replay original transport envelopes across reload to cover stale requests and reused return IDs. Also release the old contexts after new hydration and verify the new callback still works. Keep execId increasing when clearing and reinitializing BackgroundFunctionExecMap so retired handles remain distinct from newly registered contexts.
